entities.name: PMID:10392521
observations: Compared weight-based with standard heparin nomograms for postoperative DVT in orthopedic patients; weight-based dosing reached therapeutic PTT sooner: 75% within 24 h and 95% within 48 h, versus 30% and 60%, respectively, with standard dosing; 40 patients total.

source_tools.relevance: PubMed abstract retrieved by direct query

entities.name: Postop DVT faster PTT
observations: In a 40-patient orthopedic postoperative DVT study, weight-based IV heparin was associated with faster therapeutic PTT attainment than standard dosing: 75% versus 30% within 24 hours and 95% versus 60% within 48 hours.

entities.name: PMID:24831654
observations: Retrospective comparison of higher-dose versus lower-dose weight-based IV UFH nomograms in 98 neurology and vascular surgery patients; higher-dose regimen achieved therapeutic aPTT sooner and improved 6-hour therapeutic proportion, but increased supratherapeutic aPTTs.

source_tools.relevance: PubMed abstract retrieved by direct query

entities.name: Higher UFH nomogram faster
observations: Among 98 neurology and vascular-surgery patients, an 80-unit/kg bolus plus 18 units/kg/hour achieved therapeutic aPTT faster than 60 units/kg plus 12 units/kg/hour; at 6 hours, 36.0% versus 16.7% were therapeutic, while supratherapeutic values were more frequent, 30.0% versus 12.5%.

entities.name: PMID:40421164
observations: Quality-improvement comparison in 42 neurocritical-care patients, including patients with recent neurosurgery or acute intracranial disease: increasing weight-based UFH infusion from 12 to 18 units/kg/hour shortened time to therapeutic aPTT; bleeding complications were 3 of 21 in each cohort.

source_tools.relevance: PubMed abstract retrieved by direct query
